Cleanup failure retains the resource; successful cleanup follows reverse registration identity order. Terminal completion is immutable; acknowledgement validates the whole owned terminal batch before deletion.
Listener snapshots sort priority, scope order, then resource registration identity. Retired instance records remain until operation ownership references are removed.

An unobserved revision retains its earlier affected descendant obligations when another update/apply overlaps; no-op apply does not create a revision, and already-observed historical closure is not retained indefinitely.

Invocation binding metadata, definition context and intercept chain identify the exact admitted registration, not a newly visible shadow; successful admission cannot strand an unreturned operation on metadata lookup.

Collect waits for actual termination and traverses stored parent links even after logical child detachment; call-host and owner-instance records, affected references and diagnostics are removed only for the collected subtree.
